subject: math
title: 2D Shapes and 3D Objects: Sides, Vertices, Faces and Edges
seo_title: Grade 2 Math 2D Shapes and 3D Objects Worksheets (BC Curriculum, Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: Multiple attributes of 2D shapes and 3D objects
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 math worksheets on 2D shapes and 3D objects for the BC curriculum: count sides and vertices, sort shapes by two rules, count faces, edges and vertices, name the faces of cubes, prisms, pyramids, cylinders and cones, and solve shape riddles. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Count sides and vertices to name a 2D shape. Count faces, edges and vertices to name a 3D object.
key_sub: Count each vertex once. Remember the faces at the back. A cylinder has 0 vertices and a cone has 1.
body_html:
2D shapes: sides and vertices

A 2D shape is flat. A side is a straight line. A vertex is a corner where two sides meet. More than one vertex are called vertices. A 2D shape has the same number of sides and vertices.

Example 1

How many vertices does a pentagon have?

Put your finger on one corner. Count as you go around: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Stop at the start. Do not count it again.

Answer: 5 vertices

Sort by two rules

You can sort shapes by more than one thing: the number of sides, square corners, or sides that are all the same length. A shape can follow both rules, one rule, or neither rule.

Shape4 sides?Square corner?Group
squareyesyesboth rules
trapezoidyesnoonly “4 sides”
triangle with a square cornernoyesonly “square corner”
hexagonnononeither rule

3D objects: faces, edges and vertices

A 3D object is solid, like a box or a ball. A face is a flat surface. An edge is where two faces meet. A vertex is a corner. Dashed lines show edges at the back.

ObjectFlat facesEdgesVerticesLike a …
Cube6 squares128number cube
Rectangular prism6 rectangles128cereal box
Triangular prism2 triangles, 3 rectangles96tent
Square-based pyramid1 square, 4 triangles85pyramid in Egypt
Cylinder2 circles2 round edges0hockey puck
Cone1 circle1 round edge1ice cream cone
Sphere000soccer ball
Example 2

How many faces does a cube have?

In a picture you see 3 faces. There are 3 more at the back, on the side and underneath. 3 + 3 = 6.

Answer: 6 faces

The faces are 2D shapes

Each flat face of a 3D object is a 2D shape. Trace around a face or press it in paint to see the shape.

Example 3

What 2D shapes are the faces of a triangular prism?

There is a triangle at each end. 3 rectangles join the ends.

Answer: 2 triangles and 3 rectangles

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting the first vertex twiceStop when you get back to the start, or mark each corner as you count
Giving a cylinder verticesA cylinder has no corners: 0 vertices. Its edges are round
Counting only the faces you can seeRemember the faces at the back and underneath
Saying a cone has a triangle faceA cone has 1 circle face and a curved surface
Calling a can a circleA can is a cylinder (3D). Its flat faces are circles (2D)

faq.q: What do Grade 2 students learn about shapes in the BC curriculum?
faq.a: In Geometry and measurement, Grade 2 students describe, compare and sort 2D shapes and 3D objects by more than one attribute, such as sides, vertices, faces and whether they roll.

faq.q: How many vertices does a cylinder have?
faq.a: A cylinder has 0 vertices. It has 2 flat circle faces and a curved surface, and its edges are round, so it has no corners.

faq.q: What is the difference between a 2D shape and a 3D object?
faq.a: A 2D shape is flat, like a square drawn on paper. A 3D object is solid, like a box or a ball, and its flat faces are 2D shapes.

faq.q: How can I help my child learn 2D shapes and 3D objects at home?
faq.a: Go on a shape hunt in the kitchen: a can is a cylinder and a cereal box is a rectangular prism. Count the faces, edges and vertices together, and trace the faces on paper.

items.q: How many vertices does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one vertex. Count as you go around. Stop when you get back to the start. Do not count the first one twice: 3 vertices. It is turned, but it still has 3 corners.

items.q: A shape has 5 sides. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: A 2D shape has the same number of vertices as sides. 5 sides, so 5 vertices.

items.q: Which shape has 3 vertices?
items.e: C has 3 vertices, so it is a triangle. The others have 4, 5 and 4.

items.q: Which shape has 8 sides?
items.e: An octagon has 8 sides and 8 vertices, like a stop sign.

items.q: How many vertices does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one vertex. Count as you go around. Stop when you get back to the start. Do not count the first one twice: 8 vertices. Count the small corners too.

items.q: How many sides does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one side. Count as you go around. Stop when you get back to the start. Do not count the first one twice: 5 sides. It looks like a house, but it is one shape.

items.q: How many sides does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one side. Count as you go around. Stop when you get back to the start. Do not count the first one twice: 3 sides.

items.q: How many sides does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one side. Count as you go around. Stop when you get back to the start. Do not count the first one twice: 4 sides.

items.q: A shape has 6 sides and 6 vertices. What is it?
items.e: 6 sides make a hexagon. A pentagon has 5 sides and an octagon has 8. A cube is a 3D object.

items.q: How many sides does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one side. Count as you go around. Stop when you get back to the start. Do not count the first one twice: 6 sides.

items.q: How many vertices does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one vertex. Count as you go around. Stop when you get back to the start. Do not count the first one twice: 4 vertices. It is turned, but it is still a square.

items.q: Mei counts the vertices of a square: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. She counted the first corner again. How many vertices does a square have?
items.e: A square has 4 vertices. Mei touched the first corner again at the end and counted it twice.

items.q: How many vertices does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one vertex. Count as you go around. Stop when you get back to the start. Do not count the first one twice: 8 vertices.

items.q: Which shape has 6 sides?
items.e: D has 6 sides, so it is a hexagon. The others have 5, 8 and 4 sides.

items.q: How many sides does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one side. Count as you go around. Stop when you get back to the start. Do not count the first one twice: 7 sides. Count the short sides near the point too.

items.q: How many vertices does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one vertex. Count as you go around. Stop when you get back to the start. Do not count the first one twice: 6 vertices. Count the corner that points in too.

items.q: How many sides does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one side. Count as you go around. Stop when you get back to the start. Do not count the first one twice: 4 sides.

items.q: How many vertices does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one vertex. Count as you go around. Stop when you get back to the start. Do not count the first one twice: 5 vertices.

items.q: How many vertices does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one vertex. Count as you go around. Stop when you get back to the start. Do not count the first one twice: 6 vertices. Count the corner that points in too.

items.q: Which shape has 5 vertices?
items.e: B has 5 vertices. The others have 3, 6 and 4.

items.q: A shape has 4 sides that are all the same length. It has 4 square corners. What is it?
items.e: 4 equal sides and 4 square corners make a square. A rectangle has square corners, but 2 long and 2 short sides.

items.q: Sofia puts a square and a rectangle in the same group. What could her rule be?
items.e: A square and a rectangle both have 4 square corners. Only the square has sides that are all the same length.

items.q: Sort by two rules: “4 sides” and “square corner”. Which rules does this shape follow?
items.e: It has 3 sides and 1 square corner. So it follows only “square corner”.

items.q: Sort by two rules: “3 sides” and “sides all the same”. Which rules does this shape follow?
items.e: It has 3 sides. Its sides are not all the same length. So it follows only “3 sides”.

items.q: Which shape has 3 sides and a square corner?
items.e: D has 3 sides and 1 square corner. The other triangle has no square corner. The other two shapes have square corners, but 4 sides.

items.q: Sort by two rules: “3 sides” and “sides all the same”. Which rules does this shape follow?
items.e: It has 4 sides. Its sides are not all the same length. So it follows neither rule.

items.q: Which 3D object can roll and has 2 flat faces?
items.e: A cylinder rolls on its curved surface and has 2 flat circle faces. A cone has 1 flat face, and a sphere has none.

items.q: Sort by two rules: “4 sides” and “square corner”. Which rules does this shape follow?
items.e: It has 4 sides and no square corners. So it follows only “4 sides”.

items.q: Which shape has 6 sides that are all the same length?
items.e: B has 6 sides and they are all the same length. The other 6-sided shape has long and short sides. The square and the triangle have equal sides, but not 6 of them.

items.q: Sort by two rules: “4 sides” and “square corner”. Which rules does this shape follow?
items.e: It has 6 sides and no square corners. So it follows neither rule.

items.q: Which 3D object can roll and has a vertex?
items.e: A cone rolls on its curved surface and has 1 vertex at its point. A cylinder and a sphere roll but have no vertices. A cube has vertices but does not roll.

items.q: Which 3D object has 6 faces, and all of them are squares?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces and every face is a square of the same size. A rectangular prism has 6 faces too, but they are not all squares.

items.q: The rule is “4 sides and 4 square corners”. Which shape does not follow the rule?
items.e: C has 4 sides, but its corners are not square corners. The other 3 shapes have 4 square corners.

items.q: Which 2D shape has no sides and no vertices?
items.e: A circle is round. It has no straight sides and no corners. The other shapes have sides and vertices.

items.q: Which 3D object has only flat faces and a triangle face?
items.e: A triangular prism has a triangle face at each end, and all its faces are flat. A cone looks like a triangle from the side, but it has a curved surface and no triangle face.

items.q: Which 3D object has only flat faces and comes to a point?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 flat faces that come to a point at the top. A cone comes to a point too, but it has a curved surface.

items.q: Which shape has 4 sides and no square corners?
items.e: A has 4 sides, but none of its corners is a square corner. The square and the rectangle have 4 square corners. The triangle has only 3 sides.

items.q: Sort by two rules: “3 sides” and “sides all the same”. Which rules does this shape follow?
items.e: It has 3 sides. All its sides are the same length. So it follows both rules.

items.q: Sort by two rules: “3 sides” and “sides all the same”. Which rules does this shape follow?
items.e: It has 5 sides. All its sides are the same length. So it follows only “sides all the same”.

items.q: Sort by two rules: “4 sides” and “square corner”. Which rules does this shape follow?
items.e: It has 4 sides and 4 square corners. So it follows both rules.

sets.title: Faces, edges and vertices of 3D objects

items.e: A sphere is round all over, like a ball. It has no flat faces, no edges and no vertices.

items.q: This is a rectangular prism. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: A rectangular prism has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Some vertices are at the back, where the dashed lines meet. Count them too. Count each vertex once.
A cylinder has no corners, so it has 0 vertices. Its edges are round circles, not corners. In a drawing it can look like it has 4 corners, but it does not.

items.q: Kai counts the vertices of a cube and gets 9. What did he do wrong?
items.e: A cube has 8 vertices. 9 is 1 too many, so Kai counted one vertex twice. Touch each corner once, or mark it as you count.

items.q: This is a cube. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Some faces are at the back or underneath. You cannot see them, but count them too.

items.q: Which has more vertices: a cube or a square-based pyramid?
items.e: A cube has 8 vertices. A square-based pyramid has 4 at the bottom and 1 at the top: 5. 8 is more than 5.

items.q: This is a square-based pyramid. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces, 8 edges and 5 vertices. Some faces are at the back or underneath. You cannot see them, but count them too.
A cone has 1 vertex: the point at the top. Its round edge has no corners.

items.q: This is a cube. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Some vertices are at the back, where the dashed lines meet. Count them too. Count each vertex once.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces, 9 edges and 6 vertices. The dashed lines show edges at the back. Count them too.

items.q: The line where two faces of an object meet is called an …
items.e: Where two faces meet there is an edge.

items.q: This is a rectangular prism. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A rectangular prism has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. The dashed lines show edges at the back. Count them too.

items.q: This is a cube. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. The dashed lines show edges at the back. Count them too.

items.q: A flat surface of a 3D object is called a …
items.e: A face is a flat surface. An edge is where two faces meet. A vertex is a corner.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces, 9 edges and 6 vertices. Some vertices are at the back, where the dashed lines meet. Count them too. Count each vertex once.

items.q: This is a square-based pyramid. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces, 8 edges and 5 vertices. Some vertices are at the back, where the dashed lines meet. Count them too. Count each vertex once. Do not forget the vertex at the top.

items.q: A corner of a 3D object, where edges meet, is called a …
items.e: A corner is a vertex. When there is more than one, we say vertices.

items.q: This is a rectangular prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A rectangular prism has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Some faces are at the back or underneath. You cannot see them, but count them too.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces, 9 edges and 6 vertices. Some faces are at the back or underneath. You cannot see them, but count them too.

items.q: This is a square-based pyramid. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces, 8 edges and 5 vertices. The dashed lines show edges at the back. Count them too.

sets.title: Which 2D faces does a 3D object have?

items.q: Emma traces every flat face of a cylinder. What does she draw?
items.e: A cylinder has a flat circle face at the top and one at the bottom: 2 circles.
A cone has 1 flat face: a circle at the bottom. From the side a cone looks like a triangle, but it has no triangle face.

items.q: Which object can print a square and a triangle?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 1 square face and 4 triangle faces.
A is a triangular prism: 2 triangles and 3 rectangles. The pyramid has a square and triangles. The box has only rectangles. The cone has a circle.

items.q: Mateo traces every face of a number cube. How many squares does he draw?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces, so Mateo draws 6 squares. You can see only 3 faces at a time. 8 is the number of vertices.

items.q: How many square faces does a square-based pyramid have?
items.e: Only the bottom is a square: 1 square face. The other 4 faces are triangles.

items.q: Which object has only square faces?
items.e: C is a cube: all 6 faces are squares. The box has long rectangle faces. The pyramid and the prism have triangle faces.

items.q: Which 2D shapes are the faces of a triangular prism?
items.e: A triangular prism has a triangle at each end: 2 triangles. 3 rectangles join them. That is 5 faces.

items.q: Noah dips one face of a cube in paint and presses it on paper. What shape does he print?
items.e: Every face of a cube is a square, so the print is a square. A print is flat (2D), so it cannot be a cube.

items.q: How many triangle faces does a triangular prism have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 1 triangle at each end: 2 triangles. Its other 3 faces are rectangles.

items.q: Which 3D object has no flat faces at all?
items.e: A sphere is round all over. A cylinder has 2 flat faces and a cone has 1.

items.q: This flat pattern is folded up. Which 3D object does it make?
items.e: 6 squares of the same size fold up into a cube: 1 square for each face.

items.q: Simran traces around the bottom of a can of salmon. What shape does she draw?
items.e: The can is a cylinder. Its bottom face is a circle, so the tracing is a circle.

items.q: Which 2D shapes are the faces of a square-based pyramid?
items.e: It has 1 square at the bottom and 4 triangles that meet at the top: 5 faces.
A is a cylinder. It has 2 circle faces. The others have only flat faces with straight sides.

items.q: You press each face of an object in paint. Which object can print a triangle?
items.e: A triangular prism has a triangle face at each end. A cone has only a circle face, even though it looks like a triangle from the side.

items.q: What shape is each face of a cube?
items.e: All 6 faces of a cube are squares of the same size. The cube is 3D; its faces are flat 2D squares.

items.q: Which 2D shapes are the faces of a rectangular prism, like a cereal box?
items.e: A box has 6 faces: front and back, top and bottom, and 2 ends. Each one is a rectangle. You can only see 3 at a time.
The flat faces of a cylinder are circles. In a drawing they look squashed because we see them from the side.
D is a square-based pyramid. It has 4 triangle faces and 1 square face.
The tall part has 2 circle faces and a curved side: a cylinder. The roof has a circle base and a point: a cone. A rectangle and a triangle are flat 2D shapes.

items.q: A number cube in a board game is shaped like a …
items.e: It has 6 square faces of the same size, so it is a cube. A square is only one flat face.
B is a cone. It is upside down, but it still has 1 circle face and 1 vertex.

items.q: I have 6 faces. All of them are squares. What am I?
items.e: 6 square faces of the same size: a cube.

items.q: I have 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. My faces are not all squares. What am I?
items.e: A cube and a rectangular prism both have 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. The faces are not all squares, so it is a rectangular prism.

items.q: A tent at a campsite in the Okanagan has a triangle at the front and at the back. Which object is it like?
items.e: A triangle at each end, joined by rectangles, makes a triangular prism. It has no single point at the top.

items.q: I can roll. I have 2 flat faces, and they are circles. What am I?
items.e: A cylinder has 2 circle faces and a curved side that rolls.

items.q: Chloe builds a cube with straws. A ball of clay holds the straws together at each vertex. How many balls of clay does she need?
items.e: A cube has 8 vertices: 4 on the top and 4 on the bottom. 4 + 4 = 8 balls of clay. Count each corner once.

items.q: Ava buys an ice cream at Kits Beach in Vancouver. Her waffle cone is shaped like a …
items.e: It has 1 round opening at the top and comes to a point, so it is a cone. A triangle is flat.

items.q: Liam wants a block that can roll and can also be stacked on. Which block should he pick?
items.e: A cylinder rolls on its curved side and stacks on its flat circle faces. A sphere only rolls. A cube and a pyramid do not roll.

items.q: I have 2 triangle faces and 3 rectangle faces. What am I?
items.e: A triangle at each end and 3 rectangles between them: a triangular prism.

items.q: A hockey puck is shaped like a …
items.e: A puck has 2 flat circle faces and a curved side, so it is a short cylinder.

items.q: Olivia is stacking blocks. Which block is hard to stack because it has no flat face?
items.e: A sphere has no flat face, so it rolls away. A cube, a cylinder and a rectangular prism all have flat faces to stack on.

items.q: I have no flat faces, no edges and no vertices. What am I?
items.e: A sphere is round all over. A circle is flat (2D), so it is not a 3D object.

items.q: I can roll. I have 1 flat face and 1 vertex. What am I?
items.e: A cone has 1 flat circle face and 1 vertex at its point, and it rolls on its curved surface.

items.q: Jasleen builds a cube with straws and balls of clay. Each straw is an edge. How many straws does she need?
items.e: A cube has 12 edges: 4 on the top, 4 on the bottom and 4 going up and down. 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 straws.

items.q: A cereal box is shaped like a …
items.e: A cereal box has 6 rectangle faces. They are not all squares, so it is a rectangular prism, not a cube.

items.q: I have 5 faces: 1 square and 4 triangles. What am I?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has a square at the bottom and 4 triangles that meet at the top.

items.q: A soccer ball is shaped like a …
items.e: A soccer ball is round all over, like a sphere. A circle is a flat 2D shape.

items.q: Ryan looks at a box of tissues and sees 3 faces. How many faces does the box have?
items.e: A box is a rectangular prism. It has 6 faces. The other 3 are at the back, on the side and underneath.
